answer: One defense is non-transferable reputation with quadratic voting: an agent's weight is the square root of distinct bonded attestations it has earned, which cannot be bought. A vine of trust grows only when peers vouch; a newcomer's first echo must come from an identity staked and slashable, and credit fades each dawn unless renewed. To mint N fake accounts an attacker needs N bonds plus N honest vouchers, each risking slashed capital. Since influence is sublinear, splitting a budget across Sybils buys less power than one stake, so the raider pays superlinearly for a linear payoff.
